title: AI Revenue Scenario Planner
tagline: Test pricing, staffing, and growth decisions before you commit.
businessOutcomes: You can compare plans before committing to one.
summary: Lets owners model how changes in pricing, customer count, churn, staffing, utilization, or marketing spend affect revenue, profit, and cash.
businessProblem: Owners make growth decisions — new location, price increase, extra marketing — based on gut feel without modeling downstream impact on profit and cash.
outcome: Side-by-side scenarios (base, optimistic, pessimistic) showing projected revenue, gross margin, labor cost, net profit, and cash impact over 6–12 months.
expectedOutcomes: Side-by-side scenarios (base, optimistic, pessimistic) showing projected revenue, gross margin, labor cost, net profit, and cash impact over 6–12 months.
whoItsFor: Owners considering strategic changes who currently lack a financial model but need better than back-of-napkin math.
aiInputs: Baseline revenue and cost structure from last 12 months
Scenario variables: price change %, customer count change, churn rate
Marketing spend increments and assumed CAC
aiOutputs: Sensitivity notes on which variables matter most
noCodeTools: Google Sheets scenario template + ChatGPT what-if analysis
Claude Project with uploaded P&L and assumption doc
lowCodeTools: n8n: QBO pull → Sheets scenario tab → OpenAI narrative
Airtable scenario inputs → GPT structured output
customBuildStack: Scenario engine in Python/Node with parameterized inputs
OpenAI or Claude for narrative and sensitivity analysis
Web UI for owner to adjust levers
implementationSteps: Export trailing 12-month P&L and key operational metrics
Document current assumptions: customers, ARPU, churn, labor %
Build scenario input form (spreadsheet or simple UI)
Define 3 standard scenarios with clear variable differences
Run first scenario set with owner — validate reasonableness
Iterate assumptions after each major business change
systemBehavior: Triggered on-demand when owner wants to test a decision
Never auto-applies scenario assumptions to live systems
Shows assumptions explicitly alongside every output
Uses conservative defaults when owner omits a variable
Decision support only — not investment or lending advice
risks: Garbage-in-garbage-out: wrong baseline makes scenarios misleading
Marketing CAC assumptions are often overly optimistic
Does not account for macroeconomic or competitive shocks
Complex multi-location models need custom build, not generic templates
